newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Public stake handicaps Telstra - Australia govt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Public stake handicaps Telstra - Australia govt.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston said on Tuesday that telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp would be handicapped in a global sense if it remained government-owned.
"Telstra will indeed be handicapped in number of very important ways," Alston told parliament in answer to a question.

"Quite clearly what it needs is to have market accountability, it needs a share price which sends a day-to-day signal to investors, to the board, to management to make them aware of how the company is travelling," Alston said.
The Australian government wants to sell one third of Telstra for about A$8.0 billion, but is facing tough opposition in the upper house Senate.

Independents Brian Harradine and Mal Colston hold the key to the sale as the government needs two extra votes to pass any legislation in the Senate and all other non-government senators are opposed to the plan.
Alston said the US$24 billion merger of British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp demonstrated the need for Telstra to increase its competitiveness through privatisation.
"Both of these very substantial international players recognise that it's necessary to get together to combine to compete effectively in the new international environment," Alston said.

"The tragedy of course is that on the other side (the Labor opposition), we have a bunch of dinosaurs who are somehow determined to ensure that Australia remains behind the main game and remains less than fully internationally competitive."
The Senate is expected to vote on the Telstra bill in the next few weeks.
